[RARC.5.6.10] Consumption-loop determinism is the **choke point**
that makes the whole engine deterministic ([LFST.7.1.1]). If the consumption
loop is deterministic ([RARC.5.6.9]) **and the ambient inputs agree**, replay
is byte-for-byte identical.

**Ambient inputs are every input to the record that the loop does
not compute**, the clock origin and the identity assigned to an event among
them. They are defined by that property, not by a list.

⚠ **Loop determinism alone does not give byte-identical replay.** Two runs
can agree on every value the loop computed and still record different events
if their clock origins differ. So the engine must take no ambient input from
outside the run where the run can supply it: a mock clock starts at a fixed
origin rather than a wall-clock reading ([NLFC.5.4]), and an event's identity is
derived from the run ([RARC.5.8.8]) rather than drawn at random.
